hints: Differentiate the logarithm by the chain rule, including the derivative of $\cos^2x$.
Divide numerator and denominator by $\cos^2x$ so every trigonometric term is expressed using $\tan x$.
Simplify the rational expression without substituting a value of $x$.
walkthrough:
Apply the chain rule to differentiate $y = \dfrac{2}{3}\ln(1 + 3\cos^2 x)$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{2}{3} \cdot \dfrac{1}{1 + 3\cos^2 x} \cdot \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(1 + 3\cos^2 x)$$

Compute the derivative of the inside term $1 + 3\cos^2 x$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(1 + 3\cos^2 x) = 3 \cdot 2\cos x(-\sin x) = -6\sin x\cos x$$

Substitute back into the expression for $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ and simplify:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{2}{3}\left(\dfrac{-6\sin x\cos x}{1 + 3\cos^2 x}\right) = \dfrac{-4\sin x\cos x}{1 + 3\cos^2 x}$$

Divide both the numerator and the denominator by $\cos^2 x$ to convert to $\tan x$:
$$\text{Numerator}: \dfrac{-4\sin x\cos x}{\cos^2 x} = -4\left(\dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}\right) = -4\tan x$$
$$\text{Denominator}: \dfrac{1 + 3\cos^2 x}{\cos^2 x} = \dfrac{1}{\cos^2 x} + 3 = \sec^2 x + 3$$

Use the Pythagorean identity $\sec^2 x = 1 + \tan^2 x$ to rewrite the denominator purely in $\tan x$:
$$\text{Denominator} = (1 + \tan^2 x) + 3 = 4 + \tan^2 x$$

Combine to obtain the final derivative expression:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = -\dfrac{4\tan x}{4 + \tan^2 x}$$

hints: Set the derivative from part (i) equal to $-1$ and let $t=\tan x$.
Solve the resulting quadratic in $t$, then use $0\le x\le\pi/2$ to reject any inadmissible tangent value before applying $\tan^{-1}$.
walkthrough:
Set the derivative from part (i) equal to $-1$:
$$-\dfrac{4\tan x}{4 + \tan^2 x} = -1$$

Multiply both sides by $-(4 + \tan^2 x)$:
$$4\tan x = 4 + \tan^2 x$$

Rearrange into a quadratic equation in $\tan x$:
$$\tan^2 x - 4\tan x + 4 = 0$$

Factorise the quadratic as a perfect square:
$$(\tan x - 2)^2 = 0 \implies \tan x = 2$$

Solve for $x$ in the interval $0 \le x \le \dfrac{1}{2}\pi$ using the inverse tangent:
$$x = \tan^{-1}(2)$$
$$x \approx 1.107149 \implies x = 1.11 \quad \text{(to 3 significant figures)}$$
